claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: the transcription's convention is one '#' per numbering component (7. is '#', 7.1 '##', 6.4.1 '###', 6.4.2.1 '####', 6.4.2.1.1 '#####'); should be '#####'.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page IV-39 shows the heading '6.4.2.3.2 Definition of Imperative Sentence' and the markdown carries it verbatim; nothing is missing. The level is not misplaced relative to its outline: on this page the parent '6.4.2.3' is '###' and both siblings '6.4.2.3.1' and '6.4.2.3.2' are '####', so 6.4.2.3.2 nests correctly under 6.4.2.3 and is at the same level as its sibling. The claimed 'one # per component' convention does not hold in this part of the transcription (specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md: 6.4.2 '###', 6.4.2.1 '####' but 6.4.2.1.2 '####', 6.4.2.2 '###', 6.4.2.3 '###'), so singling out 6.4.2.3.2 is wrong; any defect would lie in the inconsistent depth of the 6.4.2.x parents, not in this heading. The PDF has no markdown levels, so the difference is formatting and does not change meaning or the parent attribution.
